newsitem.title: USA: SEC documents flow smoothly through backup EDGAR.
newsitem.headline: SEC documents flow smoothly through backup EDGAR.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday it saw no glitches in its backup electronic filing system, which allowed companies and investors to successfully file their documents.
Documents began moving through the Electronic Data Gathering Analysis and Retrival (EDGAR) backup computer located at the Washington headquarers about 1300 EST/1800 GMT.
Althoughh lulls in processing the filings occured throughout the afternoon, they were not caused by the system failure, the commission said.

A power failure to the main EDGAR computer system in Alexandria, Va., result in a major system failure, which precluded it from being able to receive, process, or disseminate electronic filings, it said.
The SEC will have people working on repairing the computer system over the weekend, said Duncan King, a spokesman in the commission's public affairs department.

The commission will put out a notice on Monday morning indicating where documents should be filed -- either to the main system or the backup system. King no further details on what caused the power failure.
